summary: Legacy 2004-era CGI binary with critical gaps across most modernization pathways. Containerization artifacts exist (Partial), but cloud-native architecture, open-source frameworks, managed databases, DevOps practices, analytics, and AI readiness are all critically deficient.

findings.description: Monolithic CGI architecture — single binary handles all logic with no separation of concerns. Cannot scale components independently.
No structured API — returns HTML only. No RESTful design, no content negotiation, no versioned endpoints.
Hardcoded file path dependency (/etc/pricing/rules.dat) — tight coupling to filesystem prevents 12-factor compliance.
No proper health semantics — healthcheck endpoint returns pricing HTML rather than structured health status.
Stateless request handling (new CGI process per request) is a positive cloud-native trait.

recommendedActions: Rewrite as a microservice with structured JSON API using a modern language/framework
Externalize configuration via environment variables or AWS AppConfig/Parameter Store
Implement proper health and readiness endpoints returning structured status responses

learningMaterials.title: Decomposing Monoliths into Microservices (AWS Prescriptive Guidance)

findings.description: Multi-stage Dockerfile exists and builds successfully with GCC 12 on Alpine. Basic containerization is complete.
Kubernetes manifests present with security context hardening (non-root, drop all capabilities).
No container image scanning or vulnerability management integrated into the build process.
No resource tuning validation — CGI fork-per-request model may not behave predictably under K8s resource constraints.
No Horizontal Pod Autoscaler configured — static 2-replica deployment cannot respond to traffic spikes.

recommendedActions: Integrate container image scanning (Amazon ECR image scanning, Trivy, or Snyk)
Add Horizontal Pod Autoscaler based on CPU/request metrics
Validate resource limits under realistic load; consider replacing CGI fork model with long-running process

findings.description: No modern open-source framework adopted. Raw C++ with stdio — no web framework, no HTTP library, no structured logging library.
Build system is a hand-written Makefile with no dependency management (no Conan, vcpkg, CMake with FetchContent).
Runtime uses Apache httpd (open source) but via legacy CGI execution model rather than modern alternatives.
GCC 12 used in Dockerfile (open-source compiler) is a positive starting point.

recommendedActions: Adopt a modern open-source web framework (Express.js, FastAPI, Spring Boot, or Rust Actix)
Use a proper build system with dependency management
Replace Apache CGI with an embedded HTTP server or modern application server

learningMaterials.title: Modernizing with Open Source on AWS

findings.description: Data stored in flat pipe-delimited text file on local filesystem. No database, no query capabilities, no transactional integrity.
No data versioning or change tracking. Rules edited in-place on prod with no source of truth.
Read-only key-value lookup pattern maps well to DynamoDB or ElastiCache.
Small data volume — migration to managed store would be straightforward.

recommendedActions: Migrate pricing data to Amazon DynamoDB (key-value lookup) or Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)
Consider AWS AppConfig or Parameter Store for configuration-style pricing rules
Implement data migration pipeline with validation

learningMaterials.title: Choosing the Right Database (AWS Database Blog)

findings.description: No analytics capabilities exist. Pricing queries are not logged — no data to analyze.
No event streaming or data pipeline infrastructure for demand forecasting or dynamic pricing.
Pricing domain is well-suited to analytics — query patterns, volume trends, and price sensitivity analysis could drive business value.

recommendedActions: Instrument application to emit pricing query events to Amazon Kinesis or EventBridge
Build analytics pipeline using Amazon Athena or QuickSight
Consider Amazon OpenSearch Service for real-time pricing query analytics

learningMaterials.title: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams Developer Guide

findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline. Deployment via manual scp or kubectl apply with no automation, gates, or rollback.
No test suite — zero unit, integration, or end-to-end tests. Correctness validated by spot-checking.
No observability stack — no structured logging, metrics collection, distributed tracing, or alerting.
No Infrastructure as Code. K8s manifests exist but no Terraform, CDK, or CloudFormation for surrounding infrastructure.
No secrets management — no integration with AWS Secrets Manager or Parameter Store.
No GitOps or progressive deployment strategy (blue/green, canary). Updates are all-at-once.

recommendedActions: Establish CI/CD pipeline using AWS CodePipeline/CodeBuild or GitHub Actions
Write unit and integration tests before further code changes
Implement structured logging (JSON to stdout) with Amazon CloudWatch Logs
Add metrics with Amazon CloudWatch or Prometheus with alarms
Adopt Infrastructure as Code (AWS CDK or Terraform)
Implement progressive deployment strategy with automated rollback

findings.description: No machine-readable API for AI/ML integration. AI agents cannot consume HTML output.
No data pipeline to feed ML models. Pricing queries not captured — no training data for dynamic pricing.
No feature store or model serving infrastructure. Static lookup cannot incorporate ML predictions.
Critical security vulnerabilities make the system unsafe for AI agent interaction.
Pricing domain has strong AI/ML potential — demand forecasting, dynamic pricing, personalized pricing.

recommendedActions: Expose pricing as structured JSON API consumable by AI agents and ML pipelines
Capture pricing query data for training dynamic pricing models
Evaluate Amazon SageMaker for pricing optimization models
Consider Amazon Bedrock for AI-powered pricing analysis
Fix security vulnerabilities before any AI agent integration

prioritizedRoadmap: Security remediation — fix buffer overflow and XSS vulnerabilities (prerequisite for all pathways)
Modern DevOps foundation — CI/CD pipeline, tests, observability
Cloud-native rewrite — replace CGI with modern microservice exposing JSON API
Managed database migration — move flat file to DynamoDB or ElastiCache
Analytics and AI enablement — instrument for analytics, evaluate ML-driven dynamic pricing
